items.speaker_state: Melos is accusing the ruler and challenging his treatment of men.
items.scene: Melos calls across the hall while the ruler has ordered his death.
evidence: You kill men from fear. You never give them a chance to speak.
Melos called across the hall,
The ruler ordered his death.

items.speaker_state: Melos is asking for time to attend his sister's wedding.
items.scene: After the ruler orders his death, Melos asks for three days to see his sister's wedding.
items.reaction_to_previous: He follows his criticism of the ruler by asking for a chance to leave temporarily.
evidence: Give me three days to see my sister's wedding,
Silence came, and guards grabbed the young shepherd. The ruler ordered his death.

items.speaker_state: Melos is assuring the ruler that he will return.
items.scene: After asking to see his sister's wedding, Melos promises to return to the ruler.
items.reaction_to_previous: He responds to his request for three days by promising to come back.
evidence: Then I will return to you.
Give me three days to see my sister's wedding,
The ruler smiled and said,

items.speaker_state: The ruler is setting a condition and warning of the consequence if Melos returns late.
items.scene: The ruler speaks after Melos promises to return, as Melos's friend is about to be chained.
items.reaction_to_previous: He responds to Melos's promise by requiring his friend to stay and threatening the friend if Melos is late.
evidence: Your friend must stay here. Return late, and he will die in your place.
The ruler smiled and said,
Melos had no time to speak.

items.speaker_state: His friend expresses confidence that Melos will return.
items.scene: As Melos is about to leave, his friend speaks after offering his hands for the chains.
items.reaction_to_previous: He encourages Melos to go despite the ruler's warning that he will die if Melos returns late.
evidence: Go now, because I know you will come back.
Melos turned to his friend, who offered his hands for the chains.
Your friend must stay here. Return late, and he will die in your place.

items.speaker_state: Melos urgently calls for the execution to stop and announces that he has returned.
items.scene: At the square, Melos arrives as the sword is raised above his friend.
evidence: Stop now! I'm back!
At the city gates, the bell rang for his friend's death. He raced to the square, where the sword was already raised above his friend.

items.speaker_state: Melos admits that he nearly abandoned his friend to die.
items.scene: After reaching the square and falling against his friend, Melos speaks softly.
items.reaction_to_previous: He follows his announcement that he is back by admitting he nearly left his friend to die.
evidence: I almost left you to die,
His friend turned around, and Melos fell against him.
he said softly.

items.speaker_state: His friend admits that his trust in Melos nearly failed.
items.scene: The friend replies after Melos confesses he almost left him to die; they hold each other as the last sun lights the walls.
items.reaction_to_previous: He responds to Melos's admission by saying that he nearly lost trust in him.
evidence: I almost lost my trust in you,
he said softly.
They held each other while the last sun lit the walls.

items.speaker_state: The ruler orders the sword lowered and both men freed.
items.scene: After watching the two men, the ruler finally speaks and orders them freed.
items.reaction_to_previous: He responds to the friends' exchange by ordering the sword put down and both men released.
evidence: Put the sword down and free both men.

items.speaker_state: The ruler asks how someone can earn such trust, in a softer manner.
items.scene: After ordering both men freed, the ruler asks how such trust can be won.
items.reaction_to_previous: He follows his order to free both men with a question about the trust between them.
evidence: How can a man win such trust?
More softly, he then asked,
For once, he waited for a reply instead of demanding one.
